intro:
You settle the technical limits of a vendor service from court orders, contracts, an operations manual, a mailing list and chat threads. They often disagree.

Initial specification:
- [e001] Precedence rule: when sources disagree, the order of authority is court-order > vendor-contract > ops-manual > mailing-list > chat-thread. Inside one source, the higher version wins.
- [e002] According to vendor-contract VC-1 version 1, the default log level is `level-info`.
- [e003] The vendor-contract document VC-1 (version 1) states that the hash function is `sha-256`.
- [e004] The vendor-contract document VC-1 (version 1) states that the snapshot interval in hours is `16`.
- [e005] According to vendor-contract VC-1 version 1, the minimum TLS version is `tls-v11`.
- [e006] The vendor-contract document VC-1 (version 1) states that the request tracing mode is `ON`.
- [e007] The vendor-contract document VC-1 (version 1) states that the maximum open files is `16384`.
- [e008] The ops-manual document OM-115 (version 2) states that the upload quota per hour is `1200`.

Sources, from highest to lowest authority: court-order, vendor-contract, ops-manual, mailing-list, chat-thread. When two sources disagree, the higher one decides.
Inside one source, a higher version number overrides a lower one. A withdrawn document no longer counts at all.
Every event has a label of the form [eNNN] with a three-digit number. A higher number is later in time. A later event can change or cancel an earlier one.
Some material quotes old pages or copies for history. A quote of that kind is not a new statement.
